title: Tau's provider/tool agent loop
question: How does Tau turn one user question into model calls, tool calls, and follow-up turns?
teleprompter_points: The direct answer: tau_agent.loop.run_agent_loop is the pure loop; AgentHarness owns session state around it.
The provider streams neutral events; the loop turns them into Tau agent events.
When the model asks for tools, Tau executes them, appends tool-result messages, then calls the provider again.
Steering and follow-up messages are late-injected only between turns, not hidden inside tools.
proof_boundary: Explains Tau's in-process portable agent loop, not provider quality or UI rendering.

debugger_stops.proves: The loop receives provider, transcript, and tools as injected dependencies.
A tool call is executed before the next model turn.

related_questions: How does a tau_agent DAG node use the loop?

steps.title: Harness owns transcript state
bullets: AgentHarness stores session state around a stateless loop.
run_agent_loop mutates the caller-owned messages list.
steps.source_explanation: AgentHarness wraps the pure loop with session concerns.
steps.proof_boundary: Does not explain durable DAG journals.

steps.title: Provider streams one assistant turn
bullets: The loop calls ModelProvider.stream_response.
Provider events become MessageStart/Delta/End events.
steps.source_explanation: run_agent_loop consumes provider events and appends the assistant message.

steps.title: Tools feed the next turn
bullets: Tool calls are executed after the assistant message ends.
Tool results become transcript messages before the next provider call.
steps.source_explanation: _execute_tool_calls appends ToolResultMessage objects consumed by the next loop iteration.
steps.proof_boundary: Does not prove external tool side effects.

title: Provider-neutral model streaming boundary
question: Where does Tau isolate model providers from the agent loop?
teleprompter_points: The direct answer: ModelProvider is the small protocol between tau_agent and tau_ai.
Providers stream ProviderEvent objects; the agent loop does not know the SDK shape.
OpenAI, Anthropic, SciLLM, and FakeProvider can all satisfy the same boundary.
This is why Tau can test the loop with FakeProvider without live model calls.
proof_boundary: Explains the Python protocol boundary, not any provider's external SLA.

debugger_stops.proves: The agent loop depends on the protocol shape, not a concrete SDK.

related_questions: How does the pure agent loop work?

steps.title: Small protocol, many adapters
bullets: ModelProvider has one operation: stream_response.
The output is a stream of provider-neutral events.
steps.source_explanation: The protocol defines the exact call shape consumed by run_agent_loop.

title: Canonical DAG runtime flow
question: How does Tau execute a public DAG contract durably?
teleprompter_points: The direct answer: public contracts compile to DagPlan, then run_dag_plan drives node execution and journals transitions in DagRunStore.
DagPlan is the frozen backend-neutral shape.
The scheduler decides readiness, executes nodes, validates results, and commits transition batches.
Replay rebuilds state from committed journal records instead of trusting live memory.
proof_boundary: Explains the canonical runtime path, not every public contract compiler or backend adapter.

debugger_stops.proves: The scheduler starts from a compiled DagPlan, not raw user YAML.
A node result is staged before commit.

related_questions: How does the viewer rebuild state?

steps.title: Compile to DagPlan
bullets: Public contracts are not executed directly.
DagPlan freezes nodes, edges, policies, and hashes.
steps.source_explanation: DagPlan is the validated internal runtime shape.
steps.proof_boundary: Does not enumerate all compiler inputs.

steps.title: Scheduler owns readiness
bullets: run_dag_plan resolves which nodes may run.
Join and retry decisions happen here.
steps.source_explanation: The scheduler state machine drives attempts and blocks continuation on invalid results.
steps.proof_boundary: Does not prove a specific external backend works.

steps.title: Journal before trust
bullets: The run store stages and commits transition batches.
Replay reads the committed journal later.
steps.source_explanation: stage_result records the attempt output before settlement.

title: Strict attempt-result admission
question: Why can a DAG node not smuggle arbitrary fields or fake output shape?
teleprompter_points: The direct answer: scheduler normalizes adapter-owned metadata, then admit_dag_attempt_result enforces the trusted output contract.
Unknown top-level fields fail closed.
accepted_output is hashed and schema-checked before successors can run.
Scheduler-owned diagnostics/extensions are explicit namespaces, not producer escape hatches.
proof_boundary: Explains local contract admission, not semantic truth of a model's answer.

debugger_stops.proves: The trusted output contract is chosen outside the producer payload.
Scheduler-owned metadata is moved before strict admission.

steps.title: Normalize adapter metadata
bullets: Known adapter metadata moves into diagnostics/extensions.
Producer extras do not stay top-level.
steps.source_explanation: _canonicalize_attempt_result_boundary prepares the result for strict admission.
steps.proof_boundary: Only known scheduler namespaces are preserved.

steps.title: Admit against trusted schema
bullets: Pydantic forbids unknown fields.
The trusted output_contract_id controls accepted_output validation.
steps.source_explanation: admit_dag_attempt_result validates and hashes the accepted output.

title: tau_agent DAG node dispatch
question: How does a Tau DAG node run the native agent loop safely?
teleprompter_points: The direct answer: native_agent_dispatch preflights shape/profile/tools, then agent_node_adapter executes AgentNodeRun through the normal loop.
Preflight happens before any provider or tool runs.
Only read-only tools are allowed in the native reviewer path covered here.
Settlement is mapped back to a scheduler attempt result.
proof_boundary: Explains the native reviewer/agent-node path, not arbitrary write-capable worker execution.

debugger_stops.proves: Tool/path/profile validation happens before transport dispatch.
The adapter builds a work order for AgentNodeRun inside scheduler attempt context.

related_questions: How does the provider boundary work?

steps.title: Preflight before execution
bullets: Validate prompt, cwd, tools, paths, and transport profile.
Fail closed before model or tool side effects.
steps.source_explanation: preflight_native_node rejects unsupported shape and unsafe tool policy.

steps.title: Execute through AgentNodeRun
bullets: Build work_order and ToolPolicy.
Run AgentNodeRun and map settlement back to status/verdict.
steps.source_explanation: execute_tau_agent_node is the scheduler adapter around the portable agent loop.

title: Replay-backed DAG viewer and cockpit source binding
question: How can Tau answer project questions with source ranges and breakpoints instead of vague summaries?
teleprompter_points: The direct answer: replay_dag_run rebuilds authoritative state, explainers bind questions to source ranges, and the cockpit/debugger bridge can reveal or prepare breakpoints for those ranges.
The viewer should trust replayed journal state, not live scheduler memory.
Each explainer record maps question -> cockpit bullets -> Excalidraw node -> VS Code range -> optional debugger stop.
The diagram is editable Excalidraw first; SVG rendering can come later when stable.
proof_boundary: Explains source-bound local cockpit records; does not claim live debugger execution without debugger receipts.

debugger_stops.proves: Replay starts from the committed run record and journal prefix.
The viewer surface is loopback/read-only by design at module boundary.

related_questions: How does the DAG runtime journal work?

steps.title: Replay the journal
bullets: Load committed records from the run store.
Revalidate prefixes before projecting state.
steps.source_explanation: replay_dag_run is the source of truth for viewer reconstruction.

steps.title: Project browser-safe state
bullets: Viewer modules turn replay state into bounded browser data.
